figures.title: One wide head versus eight narrow heads
figures.caption: Splitting d_model = 512 into eight heads of d_head = 64 gives each head its own softmax. The wide head must divide one unit of mass between the previous token and the antecedent, 0.497 and 0.458; the split heads each put 0.984 on their relation. The eight 64-vectors concatenate into a 512-vector and W_O maps it back to the residual stream. Parameters are unchanged: 8 × 512 × 64 = 512 × 512 = 262,144 per projection, 4 × 262,144 = 1,048,576 attention weights.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. The left panel, one head of width 512, lists Q, K and V as 512 by 512 matrices, one softmax over the sequence, two relations sharing the mass at 0.497 and 0.458, one 512-vector output, and a 512 by 512 W_O. The right panel, eight heads of width 64, lists Q_h, K_h and V_h as 512 by 64 matrices, eight independent softmaxes, head 1 putting 0.984 on the previous token, head 2 putting 0.984 on the antecedent, eight 64-vector outputs, and a 512-vector concatenation followed by W_O. The parameter note says 8 × 512 × 64 = 262,144 per projection either way.

panels.title: Eight heads, width 64
panels.note: Parameters: 8 × 512 × 64 = 262,144 per projection; 4 × 262,144 = 1,048,576 attention weights either way.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to split the layer into heads and put it back together.

steps.label: Start with one 512-wide head: Q, K, V are 512 × 512, one softmax over the sequence.
Split d_model = 512 into eight heads of d_head = 64: Q_h, K_h, V_h are 512 × 64 each.
Each head runs its own softmax, so each head gets its own unit of mass.
Head 1 puts 0.984 on the previous token; head 2 puts 0.984 on the antecedent. The wide head had to split 0.497 and 0.458.
W_O is 512 × 512 either way: 8 × 512 × 64 = 512 × 512 = 262,144 per projection.

figures.title: What survives head pruning
figures.caption: The sparse model kept 14 of 48 encoder self-attention heads, 31 of 48 decoder self-attention heads, and 30 of 48 decoder-encoder heads. The last bar is the 48-head budget, not a pruned model. Most encoder layers tolerated losing a large share of heads with a small BLEU change; the decoder was less prunable.
figures.alt: Four horizontal bars. Encoder self-attention: 14 of 48. Decoder self-attention: 31 of 48. Decoder-encoder attention: 30 of 48. A reference bar shows the 48-head budget.

data.note: Voita et al. 2019 kept these heads in their sparse model after L0 head gating. The last bar is the budget, not a pruned model.

steps.label: Encoder self-attention: 14 of 48 heads survive L0 gating and pruning.
Decoder self-attention is less prunable: 31 of 48 survive.
The last bar is the 48-head budget, not a pruned model.

figures.title: How a previous-token head becomes an induction head
figures.caption: Two layers on one column grid. Layer 1's previous-token head attends from i to i−1 and writes c_i, a copy of x_{i−1}, into position i. Layer 2's query is q_i = W_Q(x_i + c_i + r_i); the composition W_Q c_i is a 64-vector produced by the 64×64 matrix W_Q W_O^{h1}. A parallel shift puts x_{j−1} at position j's key, so the query matches wherever x_{j−1} = x_i, and the value there is x_j, the token that followed the earlier occurrence.
figures.alt: Two chains on a shared grid of six columns: x_i, attend i−1, c_i, q_i, keys x_{j−1}, value x_j. The first chain, layer 1, has boxes at x_i, attend to i−1, and c_i = copy of x_{i−1}. The second chain, layer 2, starts with a dashed box at c_i from layer 1, then q_i = W_Q(x_i + c_i + r_i), then key holds x_{j−1}, then lands on j: value x_j. Each chain carries a note naming the head type.

chains.label: layer 1
chains.note: A previous-token head: it attends from i to i−1 and writes a copy of x_{i−1} into position i's residual.

chains.label: layer 2
chains.note: An induction head: W_Q c_i is a 64-vector produced by the 64×64 matrix W_Q W_O^{h1}. The key shift by one turns a match into a next-token prediction.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to compose two layers into an induction head.

steps.label: Layer 1: a previous-token head attends from i to i−1.
It writes c_i into position i; layer 2's query reads it, q_i = W_Q(x_i + c_i + r_i).
On the key side a parallel shift puts x_{j−1} at position j.
The query matches where x_{j−1} = x_i, so attention lands on j and the value is x_j.
